task.description: The #journal table has tr.student rows with the attributes data-status ("active" or "left") and data-score (score); inside are td.student__name, td.student__score and an empty td.student__note. jQuery is already loaded. 1) Save the rows inside #journal with data-status="active" in the constant $active (attribute selector). 2) Write the text "Active students: 4" to #active-count, where the number is $active.length. 3) Add the is-left class to the other .student rows (the .not method). 4) Use .each to find the best score among active students: Number(this.dataset.score). 5) Add the is-best class to the row with the best score (in a tie - the first one in the table), write "best" to its .student__note, and "Best result: Dilnoza (95)" to #best; if there are no active students - "No active students". 6) Collect the names of active students into the names array with .map(...).get(), write them to #names separated by a comma and a space, and log the array to the console. Do not use document.querySelector, innerHTML, .html() or for loops.

tests.name: $active is a jQuery object with 4 active rows
tests.fail: const $active = $("#journal").find('tr[data-status="active"]'); - you need the tr rows themselves, not the cells.

tests.name: The is-left class only on students who left
The best among active students is Dilnoza, not Timur who left (99)
tests.fail: Look for the maximum only among $active and add the is-best class to the tr row.

tests.name: The best one's mark is "best", the others are empty
tests.fail: Find the cell inside the row: $bestRow.find(".student__note").text("best");

tests.name: #best: "Best result: Dilnoza (95)"
tests.fail: Take the name from the row: $bestRow.find(".student__name").text().

tests.name: Scores are compared as numbers: 100 is greater than 95
tests.fail: data-score is a string, and "100" < "95" when comparing strings. Use Number(this.dataset.score).

tests.name: In a tie, the best is the first one in the table
tests.fail: Take the first of the matching rows: .first().

tests.name: names is an array of active names
tests.fail: At the end of the chain, .map(...) needs .get(), and inside the function - return $(this).text();

tests.name: #names: "Anna, Bobur, Dilnoza, Elena" and the array in the console
A new active row is taken into account
tests.fail: Do not write numbers and names by hand - take everything from the table.
tests.setup: $("#journal tbody").append('Zarina80');

tests.name: With no active students: 0, "No active students", an empty array
tests.check: $active.length === 0 && document.querySelector("#active-count").textContent === "Active students: 0" && document.querySelector("#best").textContent === "No active students" && Array.isArray(names) && names.length === 0 && $(".is-best").length === 0 && __error === null

tests.name: The program runs without errors
tests.fail: Check: inside .each and .map you need a regular function, not an arrow one, if you use this.

hints: Inside .each(function () { ... }), this is the row's DOM element, and this.dataset.score is a string. Turn it into a number: Number(...).
Find the row with the best score with .filter(function () { return ... === bestScore; }).first(). If there are no active students, its .length is 0.

questions.question: What will $('li[data-status="active"]') find?
options: All li with the data-status attribute equal to active
All li with the active class
The first li with the data-status attribute
The data-status attribute of all li
questions.explanation: The attribute selector [name="value"] selects elements with the exact attribute value.

questions.question: Match the method with the direction of movement through the tree.
pairs: One step up - to the parent
Up to the closest matching ancestor (starting with itself)
questions.explanation: parent and children - one level, closest and find - any number of levels, siblings - on the same level.

questions.question: How is .filter(".done") different from .find(".done")?
options: .filter keeps only the matching ones out of those already found, .find searches for descendants inside them
.filter searches for descendants, .find narrows down those found
.filter returns an array, .find returns a jQuery object
questions.explanation: filter narrows the set without searching inside. find goes down to descendants.

questions.question: Which code returns a jQuery object with only the second element of the list $items?
questions.explanation: eq counts from zero; [1] gives a DOM element, not a jQuery object; eq(2) is the third one.

questions.question: What does $(".task").is(".done") return?
options: A jQuery object with the finished tasks
true if at least one task has the done class
true only if all tasks are done
The number of tasks with the done class
questions.explanation: .is() returns true/false: true if at least one element matches.

questions.question: What is this inside $(".row").each(function () { ... })?
options: A jQuery object with all rows
The current DOM element of the iteration
questions.explanation: this is a DOM element. To call jQuery methods, wrap it: $(this).

questions.question: Which method do you add after .map(...) to get a regular JavaScript array? Enter the call with a dot, for example .first()
questions.explanation: In jQuery, .map() returns a jQuery object; .get() without an argument turns it into an array.

questions.question: Why does the code $rows.each(() => { $(this).addClass("x"); }) not work?
options: An arrow function has no this of its own: it is taken from outside, not the current element
addClass cannot be called inside each
questions.explanation: For this, use a regular function or the (index, element) parameters.

questions.question: Rows have data-score="100" and data-score="95". What is this.dataset.score > "95" for the first row?
questions.explanation: dataset always returns strings, and strings are compared character by character: "1" < "9". You need Number().

questions.question: Which code is recommended in jQuery 4 instead of positional pseudo-classes?
questions.explanation: :first and :eq() are deprecated; use the methods .first(), .last(), .eq().

questions.question: Match the code with the type of result.
questions.explanation: eq keeps a jQuery object, get(0) gives an element, get() after map gives an array, is gives a boolean.
